newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: New Great Lakes envoy in talks in Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: New Great Lakes envoy in talks in Ethiopia.

text.p: Mohamed Sahnoun, the first joint envoy of the United Nations and Organisation of African Unity (OAU), discussed crises in the Great Lakes region of central Africa with OAU officials on Monday, U.N. sources said.
They said Sahnoun, an Algerian diplomat named last month to promote peace and direct U.N. political work and aid to the region, was briefed by OAU officials on Zaire, Burundi and refugee problems.
Sahnoun was expected to meet Ethiopian Prime Minister Meles Zenawi later on Monday before flying to Nairobi, his new headquarters for what diplomats say is a very tough assignment.

Sahnoun resigned as special representative to Somalia in 1992 after then U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali rebuked him for saying the U.N. was slow to react to famine in the Horn of Africa country.
New U.N. Secretary-General Koffi Annan has said the envoy needs an aircraft and communications at his Nairobi base and sub-offices in the capitals of Burundi, Rwanda and Zaire.

Since his appointment, Sahnoun has spoken of the need for a comprehensive solution to the Great Lakes crisis. But U.N. officials say he will need to tackle problems one by one before political conditions are suitable for an overall resolution.
